hints.title: Use the smallest right-hand side
hints.body: The inequality must hold at the corner where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></math> is zero. Substitute that input into the original inequality.
hints.recap: A carefully chosen input can give a necessary parameter bound.
hints.pitfall: One input alone cannot prove the inequality for every input.
hints.pause: Derive the parameter restriction implied at that corner.

hints.title: Check the boundary parameter on every region
hints.body: Use the boundary parameter from your necessary condition. Split the real line at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> and remove the modulus signs on each region.
hints.recap: The two modulus expressions change formula at different corners.

hints.title: Extend a valid boundary case
hints.body: For a fixed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math>, compare <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> at two parameter values, using <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>.
hints.recap: Monotonicity in the parameter can extend a proved boundary case.
hints.pitfall: You must first verify that the boundary case actually works for every real input.
hints.pause: Combine your three-region proof with this parameter comparison to obtain the complete set.

recall.reminder: Monotonicity in the parameter can extend a proved boundary case.

solution:
1. A necessary bound. At x=2, 2a+1≤0, so a≤−12.

2. Prove the boundary works. For a=−12, the gap |x−2|−(1−12|x|) equals 1−32x on x≤0, 1−12x on 0≤x≤2, and 32x−3 on x≥2. Every expression is nonnegative on its stated region.

3. Extend the result. Any smaller a lowers or leaves unchanged the left side for each fixed x. Every a≤−12 therefore works.

Answer E. The necessity check excludes larger values; the three-region proof establishes every remaining value.
knowledgePattern: Find the sharp parameter bound from the cusp and prove it globally
